page: Microsoft Azure L128aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads with extreme local disk capacity demands. Powered by AMD processors on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with no integrated GPUs present in the configuration.

The primary architectural distinction of this VM is its bundled 92159 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. By attaching over 90 TB of high-speed solid-state storage directly to the host chassis, the configuration eliminates the network latency and bandwidth ceilings associated with remote block storage volumes. A operational consideration is the non-persistent nature of local NVMe storage across deallocations, requiring application-layer replication architectures to maintain high availability and data durability.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the consolidation of massive NVMe disk arrays, substantial memory volume, and high dedicated core counts reduces the necessity for sprawling multi-node storage clusters. These attributes position the server for large-scale distributed databases such as Apache Cassandra and MongoDB, high-capacity Elasticsearch or OpenSearch nodes, data warehousing engines, transactional SQL systems, and real-time analytical platforms processing multi-terabyte data sets locally.
description: Microsoft Azure L128aos_v5 is a storage-optimized instance designed for large-scale data systems requiring substantial low-latency local persistence and compute concurrency. Built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD processors, it delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 1024 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is bundled with 92159 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators. With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and tens of terabytes of integrated solid-state storage, the instance emphasizes dense local throughput over distributed network storage. From an efficiency standpoint, packaging vast NVMe capacity directly with dense compute eliminates external storage network overhead for I/O-heavy operations. The instance is suited for massive relational and non-relational database clusters, data warehousing engines, distributed file systems, Elasticsearch deployments, and high-throughput real-time analytical processing platforms.
